title: Restriction of scalars as a ringed-topos module direct image
statement: For a small site (C,J) and ring sheaves R,S [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], every ring-sheaf morphism c:S to R induces a ringed-topos morphism from (J,R) to (J,S) [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism] whose module direct-image functor equals restriction of scalars along c.

source.place: Definition 01D3 (definition-ringed-topos), restriction of scalars and Definition 03D6

proof.text: Take identity inverse and direct set-image functors with their identity adjunction. Use c for the structural ring map. Its ring-homomorphism laws prove preservation of zero, one, addition and multiplication. Set the module functor equal to restriction of scalars. Its underlying additive sheaf is unchanged and the generalized-element linearity identity is exactly the assumed sectionwise identity. This includes zero rings and the empty site.

proof_origin.place: Extracted the already proved identity-site restriction constructor of EtaleModuleAbelianRingedPresentation (F2).

    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
